title: ADR: Configuration Entropy Mitigation and Platform Guardrails
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

Configuration entropy (divergent config, ad-hoc overrides, and undocumented local changes) has caused multiple incidents and subtle performance regressions across the Redwood platform. This ADR defines a platform-wide contract to reduce config entropy by combining declarative schemas, runtime guardrails, staged overrides, and operational telemetry. The goal is to make configuration changes auditable, reversible, and composable while preserving safe override mechanisms for urgent operational needs.

Why this matters

- High config entropy increases incident blast radius and slows incident remediation.
- Ad-hoc overrides are frequently permanent because they lack observability and rollback metadata.
- Customers on Dedicated/Private deployments require deterministic, auditable behavior for compliance.

Decision

We adopt a three-tier configuration contract plus enforcement and telemetry strategy:

1) Canonical declarative schema: Each service declares a machine-readable schema (OpenAPI schema or JSON Schema subset) for runtime configuration that includes types, allowed ranges, provenance metadata, and deprecation markers. The schema lives in the service repo under /config/schema.yaml and is validated during CI.

2) Guardrails & enforcement layer: A platform-level guardrail component (Config-Gate) enforces safe defaults at runtime. Config-Gate applies:
   - Range clamps for numeric fields (min/max enforcement).
   - Immutable fields (cannot be overridden at runtime without a staged rollout).
   - TTLs on ephemeral overrides (auto-expire after configured window).
   - Allow-listing for deprecated keys to force visibility.

3) Staged override protocol: Emergency or temporary overrides must follow a strict lifecycle:
   - Create an override ticket in the Releases/Override queue with the change, owner, and duration.
   - An operator applies a time-bounded override via the administrative API.
   - The override is visible in the Config Audit stream and must be reviewed within 72 hours and either codified into the canonical schema or revoked.

Implementation Rules

- Schema authoring: Service owners are responsible for schema completeness. Required top-level fields in schema.yaml: id, description, type, default, min/max (if numeric), allowed_values (if enum), sensitive: boolean, owner: team-slug, deprecation: {deprecated_by, sunset_date}.

- CI validation: Every pull request modifying schema.yaml must pass the config-schema-validator job which runs:
  1. Syntax check (YAML parse).
  2. Semantic checks (required fields, valid owners, non-empty descriptions).
  3. Backwards-compatibility check against latest published schema (no incompatible removal without ADR).

- Runtime behavior: Config-Gate merges configuration from layers in the following precedence (highest to lowest):
  1. Time-bounded overrides (admin API)
  2. Service runtime flags (runtime-config-store)
  3. Environment-specific values (tenant override files)
  4. Canonical defaults from schema.yaml

- Observability: Each effective configuration evaluation generates a ConfigEvent that includes: service, key, effective_value, applied_layer, origin_commit, override_id (if any), and timestamp. ConfigEvents are exported to the platform observability cluster with the config.* metric namespace and retained for 90 days by default.

Operational thresholds and SLOs

- Config drift rate: The rate of unexplained deviations from schema defaults (keys not codified in schema) must be < 0.2% of total config reads per day.
- Override expiry compliance: 95% of admin-applied overrides must have an explicit expiry within the same business day of creation.
- Audit latency: ConfigEvents must be available in the observability pipeline within 60s (P99 120s).
- Incident detection: An automated guardrail alert triggers when any experiment flag exceeds 10% of requests served without explicit schema registration.

Rollout plan

1. Phase 0 (2 weeks): Platform team deploys a read-only ConfigEvent forwarder to gather baseline metrics and identify high-entropy services.
2. Phase 1 (6 weeks): Land the schema validator in CI and require schema.yaml in a Production-ready branch for 20 pilot services (runtime team, inference-runtime, routing).
3. Phase 2 (8 weeks): Deploy Config-Gate enforcement in read-mode (no enforcement), expose ConfigEvents and dashboards, and run config chaos exercises to validate observability.
4. Phase 3 (4 weeks): Enable hard enforcement for non-critical fields (range clamp, TTL) and require overrides to be time-bounded.
5. Phase 4 (ongoing): Full enforcement rollout across all services with quarterly audits.

Operational checklist for service owners

1. Add a schema.yaml to the service repository in the config/ directory.
2. Add the config-schema-validator job to CI (copy template: //ci/templates/config-schema-validator.yml).
3. Register owner team in the schema and ensure team-slug resolves in the org directory.
4. Instrument config reads to emit ConfigEvent with the documented payload.
5. Plan a 2-week remediation sprint if the service falls into the top 25% of config entropy by baseline metrics.

Emergency override flow (step-by-step)

1. Open an Override ticket in the Releases/Override queue with: service, key, proposed_value, reason, runbook link, expected expiry.
2. Pager-duty on-call approves if the change is urgent, otherwise code change via PR.
3. Operator invokes admin API: POST /admin/v1/overrides {service,key,value,expiry,owner,ticket_id}.
4. Override is automatically annotated in ConfigEvents and visible on the platform Overrides dashboard.
5. Review within 72 hours: either codify or revoke. Failure to review triggers automated escalation to the owning team lead.

Security and privacy considerations

- Sensitive keys flagged sensitive: true in schema.yaml must never be logged in plaintext. ConfigEvent fields for sensitive keys must redact effective_value and origin_commit unless the observer has an authorized role (see RBAC section).
- Overrides and audit entries are retained for 1 year for compliance and e-discovery. Access to the override history is audited.

RBAC and Delegation

- Roles: config-reader, config-writer, config-admin.
- config-writer can apply time-bounded overrides up to 24h. config-admin can apply up to 7 days and mark immutable overrides.
- All admin API calls require x-request-id and must be traceable to a SSO identity.

Monitoring and dashboards

Key dashboards to create:
- Platform / Config Entropy Overview: daily drift rate, top keys by override frequency, services with highest ephemeral override counts.
- Overrides Dashboard: open overrides, age distribution, expiry compliance.
- Schema Coverage: services with missing schema.yaml or failing CI validation.

Example schema.yaml snippet

| key          | type   | default | min | max | sensitive | owner       | description                      |
|--------------|--------|---------|-----|-----|-----------|-------------|----------------------------------|
| max_infers   | integer| 8       | 1   | 64  | false     | inference    | Maximum parallel inferences per container |
| log_level    | string | info    |     |     | false     | runtime      | Logging level (enum: debug,info,warn,error) |
| api_token    | string |         |     |     | true      | security     | System token used for internal telemetry |

Compatibility and migration guidance

- Backwards-incompatible removals require an ADR and a 4-week deprecation window where Config-Gate will generate warnings.
- For Private deployments, we provide a configuration shim that replicates Config-Gate semantics locally; customer engineers must opt into enforcement via a feature flag during onboarding.

Open questions and future work

- How to represent computed/derived config values in the schema in a standard way (templating vs. computed metadata).
- Whether to provide a platform SDK for schema generation from strongly-typed service code.

Appendix: example admin API (simplified)

POST /admin/v1/overrides
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
Body:
{
  "service": "inference-runtime",
  "key": "max_infers",
  "value": 12,
  "expiry": "2025-02-01T18:30:00Z",
  "owner": "alice@redwood.com",
  "ticket_id": "OR-1234"
}

This ADR will be revisited 6 months after full enforcement rollout or earlier if incidents indicate gaps in coverage.
